schemaNotes: Actions are stable identifiers resolved by reviewed host adapters; the manifest never supplies arbitrary shell commands.
Persist only step versions, states, timestamps and coarse non-secret results.
Keep credentials in each application’s mutable native store; keep root Wi-Fi and Tailscale state separate.
First account action is Chrome profile sign-in, after a connection exists.
Later/skipped is distinct from verified complete.
A lease belongs to a running adapter process so reopening cannot start duplicate logins.
Re-probe live state when reopening; never treat the mere presence of a token file as signed in.

steps.title: Connect to Wi-Fi
steps.body: Choose your network and enter its password. The desktop and applications are already installed. If Ethernet is connected, continue.
steps.notes: Use the existing Domicile NetworkManager control and captive portal. Keep the password in NetworkManager, outside this manifest and the Nix store.

steps.title: Sign in to Chrome

completion.text: My Chrome profile is signed in and my saved information is available.

steps.body: Open Chrome’s profile button and sign in with your own Google Account. Check that your bookmarks and saved passwords are available.
steps.notes: This is the first account step. Do not inspect Chrome cookies or profile databases to infer completion. Do not force synchronization or overwrite an existing profile.

steps.title: Connect your Tailscale account
steps.body: Sign in using the account that will own this computer. This makes it reachable for managed updates.
steps.notes: Use browser authentication. No reusable auth key, copied node state, or Tom account in the USB image.

steps.title: Invite Tom
steps.body: Invite Tom to your Tailscale account with the agreed management role. He can then finish maintenance and verify remote access.
steps.notes: Membership invitation and machine sharing are different. The final choice of role and SSH policy belongs to the management configuration. Never assume clicking Invite proves remote reachability.

steps.title: Connect GitHub
steps.body: Authorize GitHub CLI as tarekcmahmoud and accept the mac17-dotfiles repository invitation.
steps.notes: Keep Git identity and GitHub authentication separate. Validate the authenticated login. Existing repository belongs to mecattaf until Tom transfers it.

steps.title: Connect Claude Code
steps.body: Sign in to your own Claude account in Chrome. The CLI keeps its sign-in on this computer.
steps.notes: Use the installed CLI’s official auth flow. Avoid resetting mutable auth state during Nix activation. Do not seed Tom’s credentials.

steps.title: Start your first DSH session

completion.text: I sent a message and received a response.

steps.body: Open your assistant, send a short message, and try returning to the same session after closing its window.
steps.notes: DSH session lifecycle is owned by dshd. The onboarding teaches attachment and resume; it must not create a second process supervisor.

steps.title: Connect Cloudflare
steps.body: Create or sign in to your own Cloudflare account, then authorize Wrangler. You can finish this later.
steps.notes: A Cloudflare account is not required to boot or use the local desktop. Do not imply it is a prerequisite for Wi-Fi or Chrome.

steps.title: Check your MacBook

completion.text: Keyboard, trackpad, Wi-Fi, camera, audio and Touch Bar have been checked.

steps.body: Try typing, moving the pointer, playing a quiet sound, opening the camera, and pressing the Touch Bar controls.
steps.notes: Run audio through PipeWire at low volume. Sleep/wake is a separate physical acceptance check. The UI should show unresolved hardware facts rather than marking success from loaded modules alone.

steps.title: Find an application
steps.body: Open Finder, type Chrome, and open it. Everything is also available with the pointer.
steps.notes: Consume the existing Imagine action/reducer event. Do not infer success from a screenshot.

steps.title: Arrange your workspace
steps.body: Open the workspace rail and move between two workspaces. Try the arrow-key shortcuts if you prefer the keyboard.
steps.notes: No Vim motions. Read display identities from this machine; no Zenbook Duo panel names.

steps.title: Use the terminal

completion.text: I can open Kitty, copy and paste, and leave the terminal.

steps.body: Open Kitty. Copy and paste with Ctrl+Shift+C and Ctrl+Shift+V. Ctrl+C cancels a running command. Nano is the initial terminal editor.
steps.notes: Never put a password or OAuth code in Touch Bar labels. Preserve ordinary Chrome Ctrl shortcuts; no global Control+n override.

steps.title: Make the Touch Bar useful

completion.text: I tried the default controls and know how to return to Esc and function keys.

steps.body: Use the Touch Bar for brightness, quiet volume, workspace switching and opening your assistant. Esc and the function row stay available.
steps.notes: Baseline functional row is independent of custom DRM rendering. Programmable controls follow the same Imagine commands as keyboard and pointer actions, and obey the lock screen.

steps.title: Shape your desktop

completion.text: I know where to change the shell and preview a change.

steps.body: Open the Imagine design workspace, review a small example change, and use the preview before adopting it on your desktop.
steps.notes: A matched source/engine pin and isolated preview are required. NixOS system changes and hot-reloadable shell presentation have different lifecycles.

steps.title: Your computer is ready
steps.body: Your browser and assistant are ready. Reopen setup from Finder whenever you want to finish an optional step.
steps.notes: Completed setup must remain resumable. Authentication expiration changes status; it must not rerun destructive installation or reset all setup choices.
